text:
How to Use This Case Study

The purpose of this collection of case studies is to provide an educational resource of experiential guides to demonstrate how to work through the full process of a specific type of data analysis (or use of a data science best practice).
This case study is modular, which means that you can work through the full case study as written, or choose sections that focus on the desired skills that you would like to learn and practice. The learning objective map can be used to determine which sections of the case study correspond with each learning objective. The continued learning section at the end of the case study will provide next steps and additional tasks to practice the skills learned in the case study.


Click here to learn more about the format of this case study:


Instructions


Instructions will appear in yellow tabs throughout the case study.





Definition


Definition boxes will define key terms for the case study. Other terms that may be unfamiliar will be included in the glossary. These terms will appear in the case study highlighted with purple text, and can be clicked on to see the definition, such as Definition of Term 1Term 1.




Question opportunity


Question opportunities will give you the chance to test your comprehension.


Answer

Some questions will have answers that can be clicked-to-expand to evaluate your own responses.





Reproducibility considerations


Reproducibility boxes will highlight specific reproducibility guidelines or best practices as they come up within the case study.



 Decision Point

Decision point boxes can be expanded to describe considerations around a decision that must be made in a specific step of the case study. The full set of decision points will be summarized in the decision point map.



 Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting boxes can be expanded to describe a common problem that may occur at a specific step of the case study, as well as ways to troubleshoot the problem.

Validate factual information using reliable sources.
Exercise extra caution with code in certain instances: code that installs packages, accesses or modifies files or data, uses credentials, or sends information over the internet.


Disclose your AI use (including model and versions).
Never provide sensitive data to a public AI tool.


Examples

Patient or student data, passwords, credentials, API keys, unpublished manuscripts or grants, and other proprietary code or internal documents.

Be specific in your prompts and ask the AI tool to help you understand the code.
The confidence of an AI tool does not indicate if its responses are correct. They may also agree with you when you are wrong.
AI may respond differently to the same repeated prompt. Be sure to document what you can for the sake of reproducibility.
Recognize that you may need to iteratively improve your prompt to reach the desired output.
